brief: I run two rolls of filament side by side. Build a holder where each roll hangs on its own axle so it can turn and unwind freely.
My FPV goggles should hang by the strap from a hook on the side of a base, not lie on the bench. Add a bin next to it for spare antennas.
A caddy for my bench that holds three screwdrivers standing handle-up in deep bins so I can grab them without digging.
A small hanging station: two hooks on the side flats, a roll of gaffer tape hung on one and a coiled cable hung on the other.
One drawer unit for the hall table. The tape measure lives inside the drawer, out of sight, not sitting on top of the unit.
Grow mint planted straight into soil inside a bin of the build, not in a separate pot perched on top.
A lidded box for the glovebox: a screwdriver stored inside a cell with a cover closing the top over it.
Two drawers, each with something kept inside it: a tape measure in one and a screwdriver laid flat in the other. The drawers must still close.
A desk tidy using no more than three bases in total, with two bins and one drawer.
A planter with at least two soil-filled bins, kept to 20 parts or fewer in total so it is quick to print.
A shelf corner unit of at most five bases, two storeys tall at one cell, with a bin on the upper storey.
Only one base, nothing more: a single-cell carry pot for loose screws, with a bin and a carry handle, 16 parts at most.
Two bedside drawers that open and close silently so they will not wake my partner.
A herb planter with soil in its bins that is non-toxic if my cat chews on it.
A two-storey garage tower sturdy enough that it will never wobble or crack with tins of screws in it.
A desk organizer with two bins that looks handsome next to my walnut desk and matches its warm tone.
A market-stall counter display with two drawers that pull out toward the customer side; show at least one pulled open.
A coffee corner: a bin for pods, and a mug standing mouth up on top with its handle turned toward me at the front.
A little bookend on two bases: a book standing on it with its spine facing out to the room so the title is readable.
A windowsill planter with three herbs in soil, all visible from the front of the room, none hidden behind another.
A bench hub that has a bit of everything: a drawer, a bin, a hook on a side flat, and a spike at a corner where three bases meet.
A potting station: two bins of soil, a carry handle on a cover, and a raised platform on a spike for a seed tray.
A craft cart with two drawers for paper, a covered cell with a handle to carry it, a hook for the scissors loop, and a bin for glue sticks.
A balcony bed with a pipe run feeding water, two soil-filled bins and a drawer underneath for seed packets.
A three-storey spice tower for the kitchen counter, one cell wide, with a bin on each storey.
A utensil caddy with two bins for spatulas and spoons and a handle so I can carry it to the table.
Two small drawers for tea bags with a plain lid on top of the unit.
A sink-side drying tray: two cells topped with grate covers so water runs through.
A pantry tower two cells wide and three storeys tall with at least four drawers for dry goods.
A drill-bit block on three bases in a row with a bin in each cell.
A big parts sorter for nuts, washers and screws: six cells, a bin in every one.
A wall panel that hangs on two keyhole hangers, with three hooks and a bolt-on bin for pencils.
A closed box to hide a wifi router, with a cable cover on top for the leads to come out and no open faces left.
A seedling row of three cells, each with soil and a young plant.
A raised bed of two bins that drain, both filled with soil.
A two-bin kitchen herb planter, one with mint and one with basil, both in soil.
A porch planter cell whose bin takes a pipe riser up through the floor so I can water it from below.
A desk stand: three bases meeting at a corner with a large platform on a spike there for my phone, and a bin for pens.
A low unit to sit under my monitor: three cells wide with three drawers.
A charging dock with a port in a side wall for the charger lead and a cable cover on top.
Two pairs of bases for a shared desk, each pair one body, the pairs joined only by a side connector so they can be split later.
A miniature-paint rack two storeys tall with bins on the top storey for the paint pots.
A sealed dry box for spare resin bottles: covers top and bottom held with magnets, no open faces.
A drone field kit to carry to the flying site: a drawer for props, a bin for batteries and a carry handle.
A bead organizer that tucks two notch drawers into the corners where its bases meet.
A workshop corner shelf on three bases with a bay part filling the corner between them.
A dresser display with a plate lying on top of the build and one other kitchen item beside it.
A sewing-room tower: drawers on the ground storey, open bins on the top storey, at least two storeys.
